I noticed that docs#Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup in mathlib had the surprising type Type (max (max u v) v u). Presumably this is just some quirk of the universe normalisation algorithm?

universe u v

#check Type max (max u v) u -- Type (max u v)
#check Type max (max u v) v -- Type (max u v)
#check Type max (max u v) u v -- Type (max u v)
#check Type max (max u v) v u -- Type (max (max u v) v u)

Does this matter? (it's not causing me any problems, I was just surprised).
Kyle has a patch that fixes this but it seems to break mathlib
Aah yes I see -- if max a b c is turned into max a (max b c) then this would explain it.

Yeah, touching anything about universes at all can break things in very subtle ways. My own patch was part of a larger experiment to see if being more uniform with normalization and the level defeq algorithm could improve performance (and usability!), but the results are inconclusive. I believe though that 5695 can be resolved with minor breakage at worst, using a simpler approach than in my experiment.

For the curious, one of the main causes of issues appears to be the Lean.Meta.solveSelfMax procedure. If you are unifying ?m =?= max ?m v, where v is some arbitrary level expression not containing ?m, then you can create a fresh metavariable ?m' and assign ?m := max ?m' v. However, if you elsewhere have a constraint like ?m =?= max u v, then the success of unification can depend on the order the constraints are processed. If you do ?m := max u v first, then ?m =?= max ?m v becomes max u v =?= max (max u v) v, which is true (both sides normalize to the same level expression). If you do solveSelfMax first, then ?m =?= max u v becomes max ?m' v =?= max u v, which no longer has a unique solution, so it becomes a postponed constraint. Later, the elaborator tries processing these while enabling approximate solutions, and it decides ?m' := u is the right approximate solution, rather than ?m' := max u v, which also would work. These approximations are delicate and are looking for specific forms. Also, it's possible for solveSelfMax to get into situations where it's not clear that adding further approximations would even help. In any case, it's clear solveSelfMax is helpful and an important procedure, but tweaking any minor details can make it become too active and hinder progress.

This is all to say that changing normalization to give right-associated max expressions is more subtle that one would hope.

There's a separate issue here that universe levels for definitions aren't normalized before they're sent to the kernel, locking in expressions like Type (max (max u v) v u) rather than Type (max u v). I think it shouldn't break anything pre-normalizing, since isLevelDefEq normalizes levels before further processing.
Let me also mention here that for some mathlib files, a big problem is the fact that instantiateMVars does not normalize universes. See #lean4 > kernel universe normalization issue
